ContentNode.title: Lab 3B : FET Amplifier Design and Linear Analysis [2hr]

LocaleContent.title: Lab Overview
LocaleContent.content: This lab covers FET amplifier schematic and symbol design, DC/AC simulation with bias annotation, noise and frequency analysis, and advanced parameter sweeps using variable equations.

LocaleContent.title: First Time Using Hands-on Labs?
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​

Welcome! If this is your first time taking a lab, navigate to the Appendix in the Table of Contents to review the interface and features before proceeding. For returning users, feel free to start your lab by clicking next in the manual.

LocaleContent.title: Using non-ANSI US Keyboard?
LocaleContent.content: If you are using non-ANSI US Keyboard, please click the gear icon to turn on Fix non-ANSI US keyboard layouts option.

LocaleContent.title: Split Screen Mode
LocaleContent.content: If you would like to view the lab manual in new window or second device, click the 3 dots to Open in a new window or Open with another device.

LocaleContent.title: Lab Guidance
LocaleContent.content:
It will take about 2hr to complete all the modules in this lab.

Modules are not independent, so you must go through them all to complete this lab.

Lab Module List:

  • Module 1 - Create amplifier workspace
  • Module 2 - DC - FET curve tracer template
  • Module 3 - Build the FET amplifier schematic and symbol
  • Module 4 - Amplifier DC and AC simulations
  • Module 5 - AC and DC simulation setup
  • Module 6 - DC annotation in schematic
  • Module 7 - AC data and noise results
  • Module 8 - Variable equation and parameter sweep for simulation

LocaleContent.title: Let us begin!
LocaleContent.content:
Click the shortcut icon for ADS on your screen, or use the Start > Programs command to find and start Advanced Designs System.

​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

ContentNode.title: Module 2 - Build the FET amplifier schematic and symbol

LocaleContent.title: Build amplifier schematic
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

  1. Insert ​​​​​​​DEMO_NETLIST_INCLUDE ​​​​​​​

  2. Insert demo_fet1  ​​​​​​​

LocaleContent.title: Build amplifier schematic
LocaleContent.content:
1. Change to Lumped Components palette​​​​​​​
  2. Insert L1, L2 components  . ​​​​​​​
    • Set L1 = 12 nH
    • Set ​​​​​​​L2 = 1.5 nH
  3. Insert C1, C2 components . ​​​​​​​
    • Set ​​​​​​​C1 = 10 pF
    • Set​​​​​​​ ​​​​​C2 = 10 pF

  4. Insert pins (P1, P2) ​​​​​​​ on the input and output

  5. Move component text using “F5” and clicking the symbols.

LocaleContent.title: It should look like this
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
  1. ​​​​​​​Change to Sources-Freq Domain palette
  2. Insert SRC1, SRC2 ​​​​​​​​​​​​​

    • Set SRC1 = -0.5 V

    • Set SRC2 = 3.0 V 

  3. Insert grounds  as needed.

  4. Insert​​​​​ wires  as needed.

  5. ​​​​​​​Save the design.

Because ADS supports hierarchical designs, a schematic created as a sub-circuit can be placed inside another schematic. The pins were added to establish connectivity for the sub-circuit schematic. 

​​​​​​​

LocaleContent.title: Build amplifier schematic
LocaleContent.content:
1. In the Main window, click on the   icon

  2. Name the new cell AMP_7GHz

  3. Click Create Schematic

LocaleContent.title: Symbol generator
LocaleContent.content:
​
  1. Go to the Copy/Modify tab

  2. Find System-Amps & Mixers (type “sy” in the pull-down widget).

  3. Select the Amp symbol

  4. Click OK.

ContentNode.title: Module 3 - Amplifier DC and AC simulations

LocaleContent.title: Create new schematic
LocaleContent.content:
1. Click New Schematic Window   ​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

  2. Name the new cell AMP_test_DC_AC

  3. Click Create Schematic

LocaleContent.title: Insert amplifier symbol
LocaleContent.content:
1. Drag & drop symbol for the amplifier from the Main window or search for its name in the Parts search field in the schematic.

​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

LocaleContent.title: Insert V_AC source
LocaleContent.content:
1. Select Sources-Freq Domain palette

  2. Insert a V_AC source.

  3. Wire on the input side of the amplifier.

  4. Add a ground

LocaleContent.title: Insert resistor
LocaleContent.content:
1. Type the letter “R” in the Parts search field. 

  2. Insert a resistor (CTRL R to rotate). 

  3. Wire it to the amplifier output

  4. Add a ground.

LocaleContent.title: Place wire label
LocaleContent.content:
In DC and AC simulations, to obtain simulation results, you must have wire labels, current probes and/or power probes in your circuit.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

  1. Click the NAME icon  (or menu command: Insert > Wire/Pin Label).

  2. Select the input wire, type Vin.

  3. Select the output wire and type Vout.

LocaleContent.title: Module 3 - Amplifier DC and AC simulations
LocaleContent.content:
This module contains the following lessons:

  • AMP_test_DC_AC
  • Insert amplifier symbol
  • Insert V_AC source
  • Insert resistor
  • Place wire label

ContentNode.title: Module 4 - AC and DC simulation setup

LocaleContent.title: DC controller setup
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

  1. Select the Simulation-DC palette

  2. Insert ​​​​​​​DC simulation controller 

The DC controller requires no further setup.

LocaleContent.title: AC controller setup
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​

  1. Edit the AC controller (double click) 

  2. Go to Frequency tab

  3. Set Sweep type = Single point 

  4. Set Frequency = 7 GHz

  5. Click Apply

All ADS simulation controllers have default setup values. But you usually have to specify the settings you want. Also, it is OK to combine different simulation controllers on one schematic as long as the sources and circuits are valid for all the controllers, as is the case here with the AC and DC controllers.

ContentNode.title: Total noise at input and output

LocaleContent.title: Total noise at input and output
LocaleContent.content:
1. Go to the Noise Tab

  2. Check the Calculate noise box 

  3. Use the Edit field to select Vin, click Add

  4. Use the Edit field to select Vout, click Add 

  5. Click Apply 

This will give the total noise at the input and output.

LocaleContent.title: AC controller setup
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

  1. Go to the Display tab, Scroll down

  2. Turn off the Start, Stop, and Step boxes.

  3. Turn on the Freq and CalcNoise. 

  4. Click Apply

If you always display the parameters you are using, you can edit them on screen. For example, Noise calculations can be easily turned ON or OFF this way.

LocaleContent.title: It should look like this
LocaleContent.content: Click OK to close the AC controller dialog when you have the correct settings.

LocaleContent.title: AC controller setup
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

  1. Select the Simulation-AC palette

  2. Insert AC simulation controller 

Although the simulation is set-up with a sweep by default, the next step is to change the frequency to exactly 7 GHz and then run the simulation.

LocaleContent.title: Module 4 - AC and DC simulation setup
LocaleContent.content:
This module contains the following lessons:

  • DC controller setup
  • AC controller setup

LocaleContent.title: Run the analysis
LocaleContent.content:
1. Click on the simulate icon  

Do not close the data display.

LocaleContent.title: AMP_7GHz subcircuit
Push into hierarchy edit
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
  1. Return to the schematic window
  2. Select AMP_7GHz circuit.
  3. Click on Push Into Hierarchy Edit

LocaleContent.title: Enable DC annotation
LocaleContent.content:
1. Right click the tool bar to enable the DC annotation first.
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
  1. Click the Annotate DC Voltage and Annotate DC Pin Current toolbar icons. 
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

LocaleContent.title: The DC node values
LocaleContent.content:
You should see the DC bias values (voltage and current) at each node. The minus sign (-) for current is used only to indicate the direction (out or into a node). 

​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

LocaleContent.title: Clear the annotation
LocaleContent.content:
1. Click on the Annotation buttons again.

The annotation should clear.

​​​​​​​

LocaleContent.title: Pop out
LocaleContent.content:
1. Push back to the top level when done.
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

ContentNode.title: Module 6 - Noise and AC data result

LocaleContent.title: Noise result
LocaleContent.content:
You should have these values in table below. ​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

This shows that the noise level at the output pin is about 1.8 nano volts.  It will be different at other points in the circuit.

LocaleContent.title: Noise result
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

  1. In the Data Display, insert a List  ​​​​​​​

  2. Select both (use Ctrl key) Vin.noise and Vout.noise. Add them.  

  3. Click OK.

LocaleContent.title: AC data result
LocaleContent.content:
You should have these values in table below.

The AC results are in magnitude/phase format by default while the noise results are in volts rms.

LocaleContent.title: AC data result
LocaleContent.content:
1. Insert another List

  2. Select both AC.Vin and AC.Vout. Add them. 

  3. Click OK.

LocaleContent.content:
This module contains the following lessons:

ContentNode.title: Module 7 - Variable equation and parameter sweep for simulation

LocaleContent.title: Deactivate the DC simulation controller
LocaleContent.content:
1. Click DC simulation controller
  2. ​​​​​​​Click 
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

This is something that you can also do with components if you want them available but not used for a specific simulation.

LocaleContent.title: Push into subcircuit
LocaleContent.content: 1. Push into the AMP_7GHz amplifier subcircuit  ​​​​​​​

LocaleContent.title: Use variable equation
LocaleContent.content:
1. Change the drain inductor L2 from 1.5 nH to L_val nH.
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

Now, the inductor initial value comes from the variable and has a value of 1.0 nH. It is important to keep the units as nH. Otherwise, the value would be in Henrys, which are the default units for inductance.

LocaleContent.title: Pop out
LocaleContent.content: 1. Pop out to the top level schematic.

LocaleContent.title: Use variable equation
LocaleContent.content:
1. Insert a VAR   into schematic ​​​​​
  2. Change the name (left side of the equation) to: L_val.

Use your cursor directly on-screen or edit (double-click) the VAR   

​​​​​​​

LocaleContent.title: Parameter sweep setup
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

  1. Double click the Parameter Sweep component.

  2. Go to Sweep tab

  3. Set Parameter to sweep = L_val

  4. Set Start = 1.5, Stop = 4.5, Step = 1.5 increments

LocaleContent.title: Parameter sweep setup
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

  1. Go to the Simulations tab

  2. Set Simulation 1 = AC1 (AC controller name)

  3. Click OK.

LocaleContent.title: It should look like this
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

Notice that the quotes are automatically applied. The parameter sweep is now ready. If you typed in the names on screen, you would have to type quotes.

LocaleContent.title: Parameter sweep setup
LocaleContent.content:
To sweep a variable for AC analysis, you need a Parameter Sweep component, available in any simulation palette.  

​​​​​​​

  1. Choose Simulation-AC palette

  2. Insert a ParamSweep component. ​​​​​​​

LocaleContent.title: Run the simulation
LocaleContent.content: 1. Click F7 or the icon .

LocaleContent.title: Notice the changes
LocaleContent.content:
Your list now shows the swept values. Select the lists and stretch the corner to make them wider.

​​​​​​​
